issues.title: Keyboard Esc and controller Start cannot resume from Pause; the uncommitted test hides this
issues.problem: PauseOverlay (PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS) resumes in _input on pause_game/ui_cancel. In the same frame, Main._process checks Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"pause_game") (main.gd:166-167 closing beat, 177-179 gameplay) and pauses again. pause_game is bound by physical_keycode (main.gd:1035-1041 _add_action) and to JOY_BUTTON_START. The new _send_escape test helper sets only keycode, so it matches ui_cancel but not pause_game, and 'resume returns to the same playable state' passes while real keyboards and pads stay paused. The parent probe confirmed this at runtime. The on-screen 'ESC / START TO RESUME' hint and input.mdx:15 ('Pause or resume during play') both promise this input. Re-opened code: the polled re-pause probably existed under the old _unhandled_input too. Either way, the uncommitted test rewrite now asserts behaviour that fails on real hardware, so it must not be committed as is.
issues.fix: Make pausing event-driven. In main.gd add a pause branch to _unhandled_input: `if not title_open and event.is_action_pressed(&"pause_game") and not event.is_echo(): _pause_game(); get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` (route the intro case per G-04). Delete the polled pause_game checks at main.gd:159-160, 166-167 and 177-179. PauseOverlay already calls set_input_as_handled in _input, so the resuming press never reaches Main. In ui_controls_test._send_escape also set `event.physical_keycode = KEY_ESCAPE`, the way real keyboards send it. Add a Start-button resume case with the existing _controller_button(JOY_BUTTON_START, ...) helper, and a closing-beat pause/resume case in chapter_scene_test.gd. Minimal fallback if the refactor is deferred: store Engine.get_process_frames() in _resume_game() and ignore pause_game in _process on that frame.
issues.reuse: PauseOverlay._input already marks the event handled; _controller_button() test helper; existing _pause_game()/_resume_game().

issues.title: The uncommitted font/theme work cannot be committed as is: untracked dependencies, first-import errors, no changelog, unchecked background reframe
sources: parent runtime: fresh-clone import prints 16 font-load errors
issues.problem: project.godot (gui/theme/custom), main.tscn (ExtResource Montserrat-Bold.tres) and game_settings.gd (three preload()s) all reference apps/game/assets/fonts/, which is untracked, as are containment_cage.gd.uid and settings_test.gd.uid. A partial commit would make GameSettings fail to parse and break all five CI suites. On a fresh clone the first `godot --import` prints 16 font-load errors because the project theme loads before the fonts are imported; a second import is clean, and CI imports only once. The player-facing changes (new fonts and theme, Esc cancelling a key rebind without resuming, background drawn at 960x540 offset 60 px instead of stretched to 960x680) have no changelog entry, which the project rules require. The background reframe moves the floor relative to the art, and nobody has checked that the actors still stand on the walkway.
issues.fix: (1) Commit the whole assets/fonts folder (TTFs, .ttf.import, three FontVariation .tres, game_theme.tres, both OFL .txt files) and both .uid files in the same commit as the scripts that reference them. (2) Reproduce the first-import errors in a clean clone with an isolated HOME. If they are only ordering noise, make the CI import step run twice, or fail the job on 'ERROR' in the second import log, so a real missing-font error cannot pass. If they leave a broken theme cache, move theme assignment to runtime or confirm Godot 4.7.2 re-resolves it. (3) Add a dated changelog.mdx entry: new Roboto/Montserrat typography, Esc cancels a key rebind without resuming, re-framed corridor and Records backgrounds (and the G-01 fix). (4) Take normal-renderer stills of corridor start, relay, safe point and Records with an isolated save, and confirm that feet meet the walkway. Hands-on play is still needed before any claim about feel.
issues.reuse: CI workflow .github/workflows/game.yml import step; existing still-capture approach used for the evidence set.
issues.user_decision_needed: Whether to land the font/theme change now (after G-01) or hold it until G-09/G-21 adjust the same theme.

issues.title: Android Back quits the app mid-play with no pause or confirmation (unsaved progress lost)
sources: bench: Make Android Back drive in-game navigation
issues.problem: project.godot [application] leaves config/quit_on_go_back at its default (true), and no script handles NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST. On the Pixel emulator, one KEYCODE_BACK during corridor play killed the process (android/33). This breaks the 'Back must work' rule and loses progress since the last safe point. Rated P0 because it is progress loss: it blocks sharing any Android build, but it does not block committing desktop work.
issues.fix: Set application/config/quit_on_go_back=false. Add _notification(what) in main.gd: on NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST, if a rebind capture is active call settings_menu.cancel_capture(); if Settings is visible call _show_pause_menu() (which already closes title Settings); if paused call _resume_game(); if credits are visible call _hide_credits(); during gameplay, intro or chapter close call _pause_game(); on the bare title call get_tree().quit(). Add a headless test that calls game.notification(NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST) in each state. Update input.mdx's touch paragraph ('Back opens Pause on Android') and the changelog.
issues.reuse: Existing _show_pause_menu/_resume_game/_hide_credits/_pause_game; the same router can back G-06.
issues.user_decision_needed: At the title root, quit immediately (Android convention) or show a small quit confirmation.

issues.title: Closing Settings from the title leaves no control focused (keyboard/controller players lose their place)
issues.problem: _show_pause_menu's title branch (main.gd:503-505) and the Esc/B path both call _resume_game(), which hides the overlay that holds focus and never calls grab_focus. The UI dump 04-title-after-settings-back.json has no focused control at any of the four resolutions. Whether D-pad or arrows can recover focus is unverified, so a controller-only player may be unable to reach New Game or Continue.
issues.fix: In _resume_game(), when title_open, call `$CanvasLayer/TitleScreen/SettingsButton.grab_focus()` (as _hide_credits does for Credits), skipping it in pure touch mode per G-09. Add SettingsButton.has_focus() assertions after Settings→BACK and Settings→Esc in settings_test.gd (around :46 and :55).

issues.title: Esc or controller B inside in-game Settings drops straight back into live gameplay instead of going back to Pause
issues.problem: pause_overlay.gd (uncommitted _input) emits resume_requested for pause_game or ui_cancel whenever the overlay is visible and no capture is active. It never checks which page is showing. The on-screen BACK button goes to _show_pause_menu (main.gd:102), but Esc/B skip the pause menu and unpause. I confirmed this by reading pause_overlay.gd.
issues.fix: Add `signal back_requested` to PauseOverlay. In _input, if Panel/SettingsMenu is visible: on the title emit resume_requested (G-05 restores focus); in game emit back_requested. Emit resume_requested only from the pause page. In main.gd connect back_requested to _show_pause_menu, then call settings_button.grab_focus() so focus returns to where the player came from. Give PauseOverlay `@export var settings_menu: GameSettings` instead of get_node_or_null plus reading capture_action, ideally behind a GameSettings.is_capturing(). Add an Esc-from-Settings test with the corrected _send_escape.
issues.reuse: Existing capture guard; _show_pause_menu(); G-03's back router can call the same paths.

issues.title: Return to Title leaves a pending choice live; pressing 1/2 or X/Y on the title commits it and the mirror choice writes the save
issues.problem: _return_to_title (main.gd:520-533) never clears waiting_for_choice or choice_context, which _new_game and _load_game do clear. The direct-response guard in _input (main.gd:552) checks only `waiting_for_choice and not get_tree().paused`, and the title is not paused. With the mirror prompt open, choice keys on the title call _choose_mirror() → _save_progress(), which records a choice the player never made on screen and makes Continue skip it. I confirmed both lines by reading them; this was not reproduced at runtime.
issues.fix: Add `_clear_transient_mode()`. It clears waiting_for_choice, choice_context, relay_refused and chapter_close_active and kills intro_tween and chapter_tween. Call it from _new_game, _load_game and _return_to_title, and add `not title_open` to the _input guard. Regression test: open the mirror choice, pause, press TitleButton, parse a choice_2 event, then assert the save file is byte-identical and waiting_for_choice is false. Defer the Mode enum refactor to G-46.

issues.title: Cooperative relay: the engineer must stand in a 20-unit band, and after disclosing there is no engineer-only path
issues.problem: After choice 1 (DISCLOSE), _interact_relay only accepts WOLF (main.gd:651). It keeps saying 'Step a little right and give me room' until WOLF is within 32 of x=605 (652-654), while the engineer must be within 52 of 605 (615). WOLF trails at FOLLOW_GAP 64 (m0_actor.gd:13), so the overlap is engineer x 637-657, about 105 ms of holding. On the emulator it took 3 nudges and 6 USE taps. Opening the essential door also depends on WOLF's position, with no engineer fallback. That contradicts AGENT.md ('every essential objective keeps an engineer-only fallback') and the public docs, which say an engineer path is always available.
issues.fix: (a) Let WOLF act on his own: when the engineer is in relay reach on the DISCLOSE route and WOLF is out of range, set wolf.autonomous_target_x = 605.0 (the mechanism Records already uses), show 'WOLF moves to the contact.', and complete state.activate_power("wolf") when he arrives (check in _process, or a short tween callback). (b) Keep an engineer path: in the same state, also accept the manual bypass (state.activate_power("human") plus _flash_relay_spark(false)), with a hint such as 'E: take the manual bypass, or wait for WOLF at the contact.' The remembered lines at m0_state.gd:123 and main.gd:686 already cover disclose-plus-bypass. Add disclose→WOLF-walks and disclose→bypass routes to m0_scene_test.gd. Re-test by hands-on play.
issues.user_decision_needed: Nathanial must confirm that the manual bypass stays available after the player discloses (PROJECT_CONTEXT frames the manual reroute as the refusal path), and that WOLF walking to the contact himself fits his intended agency.

issues.title: Leaving the app (Home, app switch, desktop focus loss) does not pause the game
sources: bench: Auto-pause when the app loses focus
parent: no pause on app switch
issues.problem: No NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED or FOCUS_OUT handling exists. After Home and return, the game resumed unpaused (android/42-43). The OS may kill a backgrounded app, and saves happen only at safe points. Held touch actions may stay pressed.

issues.title: Packaged builds will not carry the OFL licence text for the bundled fonts, and the credits do not name the typefaces
sources: synthesis spot-check: fonts folder and TTF name table
issues.problem: OFL 1.1 requires every redistributed copy to include the copyright notice and licence. The source ZIP will include the *-OFL.txt files once committed. A Godot export packs only imported resources unless an include filter is set, and the TTFs' name tables carry only a pointer ('licensed under the SIL Open Font License... openfontlicense.org'), not the licence text. The in-game credits and credits.mdx list no typefaces. This is not a blocker today (no packaged build exists), but it must be resolved before the first packaged export.
issues.fix: Add a 'Typefaces' block to the in-game CreditsBody (main.tscn:548) and credits.mdx: 'Roboto, Copyright 2011 The Roboto Project Authors; Montserrat, Copyright 2011 The Montserrat Project Authors; SIL Open Font License 1.1'. When an export preset is committed (G-45), add `assets/fonts/*.txt` to its include filter, or show the full OFL text from a credits sub-page. Record this in manifest.json's terms_reference.
issues.reuse: Existing manifest entries for both fonts; CreditsBody RichTextLabel.

issues.title: A controller rebind cannot be cancelled from the controller; B and the D-pad are silently bound instead
issues.problem: GameSettings._input cancels only on KEY_ESCAPE (game_settings.gd:363). Every controller button or stick push is consumed as the new binding. _binding_conflict skips ui_* actions, so B (ui_cancel) and the D-pad are accepted. The note tells controller players 'Esc cancels.' (:349), and they cannot reach CANCEL REBIND. Recovery requires RESTORE DEFAULT CONTROLS, which also resets keyboard bindings. Rated P2 because rebinding is not on the core play path.
issues.fix: During a controller capture, treat JOY_BUTTON_START as cancel unless Pause itself is being rebound (Start can never be another action's binding because the conflict check rejects it). Alternatively, treat a ~0.6 s B hold as cancel, which keeps B bindable as settings_test.gd:88 expects. Make the note device-specific: 'Press a key for X. Esc cancels.' / 'Press a button or stick direction for X. START cancels.' Update settings.mdx:26 and add a controller-cancel test.
issues.user_decision_needed: Which controller input cancels a capture: Start (recommended) or a B hold.

issues.title: Any rebind silently deletes that action's alternate bindings (Left arrow, D-pad or stick)
issues.problem: _replace_binding (game_settings.gd:400-404) erases every event of that kind before adding the new one. Rebinding Move left on keyboard drops the Left-arrow alternate along with A. On controller it removes both the D-pad and left-stick bindings. There is no warning.
issues.fix: Replace only the event shown in the clicked slot: pass the old event from the binding button into begin_capture and erase only that one. Alternatively add an explicit second 'ALT' column. Add a test that the Left arrow survives a keyboard rebind of move_left.
issues.reuse: binding_label()/binding buttons already know their event list.

issues.title: Rebinding shows no 'listening' state on the binding being changed

issues.title: Controller prompts use Xbox letters on every pad, raw 'AXIS n' text, mixed Esc/Escape names, and truncated controller bindings
issues.problem: _button_label returns A/B/X/Y/START regardless of device, so on Nintendo pads the prompts name the wrong buttons and on PlayStation pads the names are unfamiliar. prompt() returns 'AXIS %d −/+' for stick bindings. The tutorial hard-codes 'STICK / D-PAD MOVE'. Prompts say 'Escape' while the rebind note says 'Esc'. Controller binding buttons are 206 px wide with an ellipsis, and the full text appears only in a mouse tooltip ('D-pad right / Left stic…', 03-title-settings-tab2.png).
issues.fix: Add one display-name helper in GameSettings used by both prompt() and binding_label(). It should map KEY_ESCAPE to 'Esc', uppercase keyboard names, use stick wording ('L-STICK ←/→') instead of AXIS n, and use device-aware button names from Input.get_joy_name(device) (Sony: Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle/Options; Nintendo: swapped letters and +; Xbox fallback). Track the last joypad device in main._input. Build the tutorial move label from prompt(&"move_left", true)/prompt(&"move_right", true). Widen the binding columns or show the first binding plus '+1'. Update settings_test.gd:96/:116 ('AXIS 2 −').
issues.reuse: Existing binding_label 'Left stick' wording; controller_active detection.

strengths: M0State is a pure RefCounted model with guarded, bool-returning transitions. from_dict validates every save field by type and range and enforces cross-field invariants, including legacy v1 migration.
Saves go through write-to-.tmp, flush/error check and rename (atomic on macOS, Linux and iOS). A failed first-checkpoint save rolls back and tells the player.

Saved preferences are validated (GameSettings.number()/boolean() reject wrong types and non-finite values, the FPS list is whitelisted, values are clamped), and bindings are bounds-checked and conflict-checked on load.
Pause hygiene: only PauseOverlay is PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, and _pause_game releases held move/interact/choice actions. All 14 tween slots are killed before re-creation.
The uncommitted pause_overlay.gd capture guard correctly stops Esc during a key rebind from resuming the game (headless test added).
Both essential gates encode an engineer-only fallback in state after a refusal (relay bypass, manual mirror port), and WOLF's cooperation never transfers control. The gap after disclosure is G-08.

Remembered choices are quoted accurately, refusal carries no penalty, there are no engineer pronouns, WOLF is consistently he/him, no private plot specifics appear in strings or baked art, and the credits name Nathanial Henniges and disclose AI-assisted production.
Dialogue is player-paced (intro, choices and closing beat wait indefinitely), and the credits roll has PAUSE SCROLL.
Dialogue and hint panels are highly readable (story text about 19.6-20.1:1, hints about 13.6:1 measured from pixels), and speaker names are text as well as colour.
Prompts follow remapping and input mode across keyboard, controller and touch, and direct response bindings beat native focused-button accept (covered by native-event tests).
Settings focus is drawn inside controls (2 px #8de5f5, 9.65:1). Rebinding offers conflict naming, RESTORE DEFAULT CONTROLS and persistence.
The pause menu is clear and honest ('Returning keeps your last checkpoint. Unsaved progress will be lost.'). The Audio tab states that no audio tracks exist yet.
Touch move/USE targets are generous (73x69 and 90x69 dp) and touch choices are large numbered buttons. Mobile disables desktop-only window options with an explanatory note.
The layout holds at 960x540, 1920x937, 2340x937 and 1024x768 apart from the noted touch label, GPU line and controller-binding truncation.
Headless suites instantiate the real main.tscn with per-process save and settings paths. CI pins Godot 4.7.2 with a sha256 check, and the last 8 runs on main were green.

issues.title: New web fonts ship as 1.23 MB of full variable TTF: untracked, no subset, WOFF2, preload or metric fallback
issues.problem: The uncommitted @font-face rules (global.css:5-19) load Roboto-Variable.ttf (489 KB) and Montserrat-Variable.ttf (745 KB) on every route: full Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese coverage, an unexposed Roboto wdth axis, no unicode-range, no preload (out/index.html has 0) and no size-adjusted fallback. In the throttled phone runs the fonts finish at about 13.9 s and 17.8 s. public/fonts/ is untracked, so committing global.css on its own would make every font request 404.
issues.fix: Follow the RVD 3.6 plan. (1) Subset each font to Latin U+0000-00FF plus U+2010-2027, U+2190-2199, U+00B7/00A9/00D7 (this keeps · © × – — ← ↑ → ↓ ↗). Use `pyftsubset … --flavor=woff2 --layout-features=kern,liga,tnum`, pin Roboto `wdth=100` with `fonttools varLib.instancer`, and limit the wght axis to Roboto 400-700 and Montserrat 500-800 (650/700 are in use; 800/900 were only used by dead CSS). (2) Load both with `next/font/local` in app/layout.tsx, for example `localFont({ src: './fonts/Roboto-latin.woff2', weight: '400 700', variable: '--font-roboto', display: 'swap' })` and the same for Montserrat, with `${roboto.variable} ${montserrat.variable}` on `<html>`. This gives hashed URLs, preload and an Arial-adjusted fallback. (3) Map the variables in `@theme inline { --font-sans: var(--font-roboto), …; --font-heading: var(--font-montserrat), … }`. (4) Delete the @font-face blocks and public/fonts/*.ttf, keep the OFL texts next to the WOFF2 files, and record the derivatives in manifest.json. (5) Record the byte delta and re-run the perf capture. The game's copies in apps/game/assets/fonts are unaffected.
issues.reuse: The sibling sonapin project already ships Latin-subset WOFF2 of these families (landing-ux note), which could avoid a tool install. Next's built-in next/font needs no new dependency.
issues.user_decision_needed: fontTools is not installed and installs need approval. Either approve a pip install of fonttools/brotli for a one-off subset, or reuse the sonapin WOFF2 files after confirming their coverage includes the arrows and · used on the site. Also decide whether to commit the fonts now as a stopgap (they must be tracked either way) or block the commit on WOFF2.

issues.title: Tailwind migration steps 3-8: move marketing.css, docs-guide.css and glass.css to utilities plus a small @layer components set
issues.problem: The user decided the docs site should mostly use Tailwind. Today there are 1,297 lines of bespoke CSS and 48 distinct marketing-* classes. The Story/Gameplay/Downloads list is written three times, the brand twice, and the SEO strings in several places. Docs screenshot figures keep the prose img margin (32px bands, RVD-15), because `.guide-screenshot img` does not reset it.
issues.fix: Follow RVD 3.5 and 3.8. Ship each step separately and verify each with types:check, build and capture.cjs at 5 viewports x 2 themes. (5) Leaf client components to utilities: ThemeToggle (`inline-flex h-11 items-center gap-2 whitespace-nowrap`), MarketingNavigation (icon bars via `group-data-[open=true]:translate-y-1.5 rotate-45`, `hidden desk:flex` / `desk:hidden`, no :has margins), Downloads (with the S-14 redesign). (6) page.tsx, one section per commit: header → hero (`dark` class, keyart `absolute inset-0 -z-20 size-full object-cover object-[25%_center] tab:max-desk:object-left max-tab:h-80 max-tab:mask-b-from-60%`) → story/progress (`grid gap-10 tab:grid-cols-2 desk:gap-20 py-18 tab:py-28`) → play → progress → footer (`flex flex-col items-start gap-1 text-meta`). Use a `<Container>` helper `mx-auto w-[min(100%_-_2rem,var(--container-site))] tab:w-[min(100%_-_4rem,var(--container-site))]`, skip-link `fixed left-4 -top-16 z-[100] focus:top-4 bg-den-50 text-den-850 px-4 py-3`, and anchors `scroll-mt-28 max-tab:scroll-mt-38`. Render the section links from one non-client `landingSections` module as plain `<a>`, and centralise `siteName` and `absoluteUrl()` in lib/seo.ts (WEB-5). `@layer components`, added only at the second use: .hud-label, .wordmark (+ `b` accent), .panel, .hud-rule (3px accent left border), .btn/.btn-primary/.btn-secondary, .link-inline, .stage-scrim. (7) Docs: `<Cards>/<Card>` from defaultMdxComponents wrapped in `<nav aria-label>`; a `<Screenshot src caption href>` MDX component built with `not-prose panel overflow-hidden` (fixes RVD-15 and carries the S-21 a11y fix); delete docs-guide.css. (8) Delete marketing.css; `grep -r "marketing-" app` should return 0. Budget: about 200 hand-written CSS lines and ≤20 KB gzip render-blocking CSS per route. Tailwind puts landing utilities into the shared bundle, so check out/_next/static/chunks/*.css after each step. `@layer base`: h1-h4 font-display, no global `a` or `button` rules, `motion-safe:scroll-smooth` on html, and a prefers-reduced-motion guard covering Fumadocs `animate-fd-*`. Re-run the contrast, target and focus checks after each section so existing fixes carry over.

strengths: Honest public copy: 'Source build available · No public release date', 'Provisional key art · Not a gameplay capture', dated archive captions, no fake download links or waitlists. The benchmark review rates this more honest than every reference site.

Project rules are reflected in the copy: the engineer is the sole player character, WOLF is independent and can refuse, there is an engineer-only manual route, and Nathanial Henniges' creative credit plus the AI-assistance disclosure appear consistently in the footer, README, about, credits and legal pages and in game.

The new mobile menu uses a correct disclosure pattern: a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, a hidden nav, Escape returning focus, outside-press and focus-out closing it, and listeners attached only while open (Playwright states.landingMenu).
Contrast is strong. Across 56-58 captures the only failure is the light-mode footer '//' (S-06). Hero copy over the key art was sampled and measured, not assumed.

issues.title: Escape or controller Start cannot resume from the pause menu (runtime-confirmed regression), and the new test cannot catch it
sources: static:tests-ci/TEST-5 (root cause of the test gap)
issues.problem: The uncommitted pause_overlay.gd moves resume handling from _unhandled_input to _input. PauseOverlay emits resume_requested and main._resume_game() unpauses. In the same frame, main._process (main.gd:177, and :166 in the closing beat) polls Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"pause_game") and pauses again. set_input_as_handled() does not affect polling. The parent's runtime probe confirmed this: with a real Escape (physical_keycode) or controller Start, the second press leaves paused=true with the overlay visible. The new ui_controls_test._send_escape sets only event.keycode. pause_game is bound by physical_keycode (main.gd:1061-1062), so the synthetic event matches only the built-in ui_cancel, and the test asserting 'resume returns to the same playable state' passes while the real control is broken. This is a broken core control introduced by uncommitted code (Pause must work during play per AGENT.md).
issues.fix: Game fix (owned with game-area BUG-1, implement once): in main.gd add `var resume_frame: int = -1`, set `resume_frame = Engine.get_process_frames()` in _resume_game(), and in _process skip the pause_game checks at :166 and :177 when `Engine.get_process_frames() == resume_frame`. The cleaner alternative is to handle the pause toggle in one event callback instead of PauseOverlay._input plus _process polling. Keep the new capture guard in pause_overlay.gd, since Escape must still cancel a rebind without resuming. Test fix: replace _send_escape with a key helper that sets both `keycode` and `physical_keycode` (copy settings_test.gd `_key()`; it moves into the shared test_support.gd in P-09). Add a second resume assertion that uses `_controller_button(JOY_BUTTON_START, true/false)` via Input.parse_input_event, and assert that pausing again on the next frame still works. Do not commit pause_overlay.gd or ui_controls_test.gd until the realistic-event test passes. Hands-on play in a normal window with a separate test save is still required before claiming the control works.
issues.reuse: settings_test.gd _key() (sets keycode and physical_keycode); ui_controls_test.gd _controller_button(); the existing resume assertions in ui_controls_test.gd:69-76
issues.user_decision_needed: Choose between the minimal resume-frame guard and consolidating the pause toggle into a single input callback (larger change, removes the class of bug).

issues.title: Uncommitted font/theme change only works if the untracked fonts, .import, .tres and .uid files ship in the same commit; a fresh clone's first import prints 16 font-load errors
sources: parent:runtime fresh-clone import (16 font-load errors, second import clean)
static:tests-ci notes/unverifiable (partial commit would fail CI)
issues.problem: project.godot now sets `[gui] theme/custom="res://assets/fonts/game_theme.tres"`. game_settings.gd:4-6 preloads Roboto-Regular.tres, Montserrat-Semibold.tres and Montserrat-Bold.tres. Everything under apps/game/assets/fonts/ (TTFs, .ttf.import, FontVariation .tres, game_theme.tres, OFL texts) and apps/docs/public/fonts/ is untracked. Committing the modified scripts without that folder makes every preload fail to parse, so all five suites fail in CI. Even with everything committed, the parent observed 16 font-load errors on a fresh clone's first `--import`, because the project theme loads before the fonts are imported; a second import is clean. CI always imports a fresh clone, so the error spam shows up on every run and would trip the zero-error log gate proposed in P-05. Separately, containment_cage.gd.uid and settings_test.gd.uid were never committed although their scripts are, so every clone generates different UIDs. The working tree on main also mixes four unrelated change sets (site CSS/nav, fonts/theme, sprite re-exports plus manifest, gameplay scripts).
issues.fix: (1) Split the working tree into focused commits or PRs, as REPO-3 suggests: (a) fonts + .import + .tres + OFL texts + game_theme.tres + project.godot [gui] + game_settings.gd font lines + both .uid files + manifest font entries + licence/credits doc updates (P-04); (b) sprite re-exports + manifest sprite entries (after P-11); (c) pause/input change + test (after P-01); (d) landing CSS/navigation + MDX captions + changelog entry (cross-area DOC-5). (2) Fix the first-import errors. Option A: remove `gui/theme/custom` from project.godot and apply the theme at runtime in main.gd _ready (`get_tree().root.theme = preload("res://assets/fonts/game_theme.tres")`), so nothing loads the theme during --import; the cost is that the editor loses the project-theme preview. Option B: keep the project setting and run `--import` twice in game.yml and the local runner (P-07), gating logs only on the second pass. (3) Add a CI guard after import: `test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- apps/game)"`, so new untracked .uid or .import files fail the build. Re-run the five headless suites and docs build on each split commit before pushing.
issues.reuse: Existing game.yml Import step; manifest font entries already written in the working tree
issues.user_decision_needed: Option A (runtime theme, clean import, no editor preview) vs Option B (keep project theme, double import in CI). Also confirm the commit/PR split and whether these go through PRs (see P-06).

issues.title: A runtime error inside a test hangs CI until the 15-minute timeout with no logs, and SCRIPT ERRORs in game code never fail a run
issues.problem: A spot-check confirms each scene test starts with `_initialize -> call_deferred("_run")` and exits only through `quit(...)` at the end of _run (for example settings_test.gd:7-8, :150). A GDScript runtime error, such as a null node path after a main.tscn rename (main.tscn is being edited in the working tree), aborts the coroutine, and the headless process idles until the job-level `timeout-minutes: 15`. GitHub reports that as cancelled, so the `if: failure()` artifact step (game.yml:45) does not upload logs. Errors raised inside game signal handlers are printed but never fail a step. Rated P1 because CI is the only automated safety net and both failure modes hide or delay real breakage. Runtime confirmation of the hang is still pending.
issues.fix: (1) Add a watchdog in the shared test helper (P-09), called from each test's _initialize: `create_timer(120.0).timeout.connect(func() -> void: push_error("test timed out"); quit(2))`. (2) Add `timeout-minutes: 3` to each Godot step in game.yml (or to the single runner step from P-07). (3) Since logs are already tee'd, fail the step on engine errors: `&& ! grep -nE 'SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error|^ERROR:' "$RUNNER_TEMP/wolf-check-<name>.log"`. Apply it to Import only after P-02 removes the first-import font errors. (4) Change the artifact condition to `if: failure() || cancelled()`. Verify by temporarily breaking a node path on a branch and confirming a fast red step with an uploaded log.
issues.reuse: Existing tee'd log files and failure-artifact step in game.yml

issues.title: Settings are parsed with ConfigFile.load, so a crafted settings.cfg can construct engine objects and run a script at game start
issues.problem: A spot-check confirms all four call sites use `ConfigFile.new(); config.load(settings_path)` on user://settings.cfg: main.gd:400-401 (_setup_settings, run from _ready), main.gd:454-455, game_settings.gd:32-33 and game_settings.gd:501-502. A reviewer traced the Godot 4.7.2-stable source and found that ConfigFile parses through VariantParser with no resource parser. Its `Object(Type, ...)` and `Resource("path")` forms instantiate objects and load scripts during parsing, before GameSettings.number()/boolean() validate anything. A settings file a player is given (a 'controller preset') plus a script beside it could run code with the player's privileges on every launch. Saves are safe: they use JSON plus M0State.from_dict. Rated P1, not P0, because exploitation needs social engineering and no distributed builds exist, but it must be fixed before the first release. The engine behaviour has not been proven at runtime.
issues.fix: First add the failing test in settings_test.gd: write raw text `[video]\nfps_limit=Object(RefCounted,"script":Resource("user://evil-<pid>.gd"))` plus a script whose _static_init sets an Engine meta flag, launch a game instance, and assert that the flag stays unset and defaults load. If it reproduces, add `static func load_config(path: String) -> ConfigFile` to GameSettings. It should open with FileAccess (the same pattern as M0State.load_from_disk), return an empty ConfigFile when the file is missing, over about 64 KiB, or matches `\b(Object|Resource|SubResource|ExtResource)\s*\(`, and otherwise call `config.parse(text)`. Replace all four `config.load(settings_path)` call sites. Longer term, optionally move settings to JSON validated like M0State.from_dict.
issues.reuse: M0State.load_from_disk FileAccess pattern (m0_state.gd:249-261); GameSettings.number()/boolean() validators; settings_test corrupt-file default expectations

issues.title: No test covers corrupt save files, failed saves or failed loads, which is the data-loss guard code
issues.problem: m0_state_test covers from_dict rejections and a valid round trip, but never feeds load_from_disk a damaged file (non-JSON, truncated, empty, array root, leftover .tmp). No test forces save_to_disk to fail, so the checkpoint rollback at main.gd:693-696 and the 'could not save' prompt are never exercised, and _load_game with a missing or corrupt file is untested. A refactor could start crashing on a damaged save, or mark a checkpoint reached that was never written, and CI would stay green.
issues.fix: In m0_state_test, write each malformed body to a per-PID user:// path with FileAccess and assert `load_from_disk(path) == null`. In a scene test, set save_path to `user://missing-dir-%d/save.json` (parent missing, so the write fails), reach the checkpoint, and assert `not state.checkpoint_reached` and that the status contains 'could not save'. Write garbage to the save path before add_child and assert continue_button.disabled; call _load_game() and assert the state is unchanged and the message shows. In settings_test, save `[video\nfps_limit=` and assert the defaults load. Use make_game from P-09.

issues.title: Test helpers are duplicated and inconsistent; some test instances fall back to the player's real save path, and test runs leave files in the real Godot user-data folder
sources: prior audit: docs/duplicates-audit.md MEDIUM 'Scene tests duplicate the same input-driver behavior' (still open)
issues.problem: Spot-check: in settings_test.gd, `reloaded` (line 112-113) and `swapped_game` (137-138) set only settings_path, so save_path defaults to M0State.SAVE_PATH = user://m0-save.json, the developer's real save. _ready reads it (main.gd:110), so test behaviour depends on the developer's own progress, and any future assertion that reaches a checkpoint would overwrite it. _new_game does not write, so no data loss today. The parent found leftover per-PID test files in the real app_userdata folder, meaning cleanup does not run when a test aborts. _tap and _walk_to are byte-identical in the two scene suites; _controller_button is duplicated; the new _send_escape builds key events differently from settings_test._key (the root of P-01); failure policies differ. This violates the 'separate test save' rule (AGENT.md:18).

It should provide: make_game(tree, prefix) -> Node2D, which always sets both save_path and settings_path under a per-PID prefix before add_child and registers them for cleanup; cleanup(); tap(); walk_to() (always releases the action); key(code, pressed), which sets keycode and physical_keycode; button(index, pressed); expect_eq(actual, expected, label), which prints both values; and the P-05 watchdog. Use make_game for every instantiation, including settings_test's reloaded and swapped_game. In the local runner (P-10), point HOME (macOS) / XDG_DATA_HOME (Linux) at a temp directory so test runs never touch the real user-data folder, as the parent's isolated-HOME run did. Then delete the leftover files by hand.
